title: Flip geodesics (FlipOut) port: tighten a surface loop or path to a locally shortest geodesic
description: Port Sharp & Crane 2020 'You Can Find Geodesic Paths in Triangle Meshes by Just Flipping Edges' (FlipOut) to Java as the curve-tightening primitive every ring workflow step uses: skeleton-region boundaries (CRAW-22), user/agent loops through picked points (CRAW-23) and loops transferred between scans (CRAW-24) all arrive as rough edge paths and must become tight necks. Data/algorithm split: `IntrinsicTriangulation` (signpost data structure over a MeshTopology: intrinsic edge lengths, signpost angles, vertex-to-face correspondence; public fields, no nested types) and `FlipGeodesics` (the algorithm: for each path vertex with a wedge angle < pi, flip the edges inside the wedge in order until the wedge is > pi on both sides; loop variant with no fixed endpoints; convergence = every wedge straight within epsilon). Output is an intrinsic path; provide `IntrinsicPathTracer` to trace it back to an extrinsic polyline on the input surface (barycentric points per crossed edge) and `ConformingLoopSnap` to produce the nearest conforming edge cycle on the original mesh for consumers that need edge marks (EdgeMarks/mark_edges, PATCH-89 forced arcs, delete_geometry cuts). Expose as a `tighten_path(geometry, path, closed, iterations)` node under nodes/selection producing both the polyline (curve output) and a per-edge BoolField. Never decimate; must run on a 936k-triangle scan loop in seconds. Use double math and reusable int/double buffers; no nested classes/records/enums, no System.getProperty knobs. Reference implementation in geometry-central.
definition-of-done: 1. Unit: a wobbly Dijkstra loop around a torus tube tightens to a loop whose length is within 0.5% of the analytic minimal meridian; every wedge angle is at least pi within floating-point error except at most one vertex, whose kink is bounded by that vertex's angle defect (a closed loop must pass through a vertex; Sharp & Crane 2020). 2. Unit: an open path between two points on a sphere tightens to within 0.5% of the great-circle distance with every interior wedge at pi within 1e-6. 3. Unit: tightening the same seed twice yields a byte-identical polyline. 4. Benchmark on the full-resolution IMG_4109.glb: FlipOut on the largest realistic ring (the body girth, ~450 seed edges, ~120k flips) completes in under 100 ms warm, with intrinsic-triangulation setup timed and reported separately. 5. tighten_path node documented; fixture dsl/fixtures/torus_tighten_loop.dsl validates with mesh-dsl-validate. 6. Launch entry 'CRAW-21: Tighten Loop (torus)' shows seed and tightened loops in contrasting colors; screenshot under tmp/. 7. Build checkstyle-green; unit tests do not load meshes from disk.

changes-made: IntrinsicTriangulation (ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/geometry/mesh/data/paths/IntrinsicTriangulation.java): signpost intrinsic triangulation over a MeshTopology - twin-paired half-edge arrays, intrinsic edge lengths, unrescaled CCW signpost angles, vertex angle sums, wedge side-angle query and the convex-diamond edge flip that keeps lengths and signposts current

FlipGeodesics (data/paths/FlipGeodesics.java): the FlipOut algorithm - open path and closed loop, smallest-wedge-first priority queue, wedge clearance test, single-edge and two-segment loop cases, plus a re-measure sweep so the run only stops when a full pass over the live wedges changes nothing

IntrinsicPathTracer + TracedSurfacePath (data/paths/): traces each intrinsic half-edge back onto the source surface by unfolding triangles, emitting a polyline with per-point vertex or crossed-edge-plus-fraction correspondence; verified to match the intrinsic length to 4e-9 relative on the torus

ConformingLoopSnap (data/paths/ConformingLoopSnap.java): snaps a traced geodesic to the nearest conforming edge cycle on the source mesh as per-edge-id marks, joining snapped points with a bounded Dijkstra walk so no vertex is inserted
GeodesicSeedPath (data/paths/GeodesicSeedPath.java): chains shortest edge walks through surface waypoints into the rough seed FlipOut starts from

tighten_path node (nodes/selection/TightenPathNode.java): geometry, path (semicolon-separated x,y,z waypoints), closed, iterations (-1 straight, 0 seed only, n capped) and label; outputs the geodesic polyline in the curve slot, the snapped cycle in the edge-marks slot and a per-edge BoolField selection. Documented in socketDocs; mesh-node-catalog.json regenerated
dsl/fixtures/torus_tighten_loop.dsl: seed and tightened loop on one carrier under two edge-mark labels; mesh-dsl-validate reports valid=true, 3 nodes, 0 errors, 0 warnings

MeshNodeViewerScene: minimal overlay that draws every boolean edge-marks label from the graph's output bundle as its own coloured feature-edge category (amber seed, cyan tightened), on both the initial and reload DSL paths
